title: [spec-gap][R-11-011/012/016] Rust LCI node server is a stub: WKC advertises nonexistent resources; /status /keys config family absent; BLE UUID diverges from NUS
description: Spec 17.5/17.3.2: node exposes CoAP server on UDP 5683 with /.well-known/core listing its actual resources; /status, /status/neighbors, /status/routes, /keys, /config/radio, /config/identity are node resources; BLE LCI should use NUS UUID 6E400001-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E. Classification: divergent (Rust stack). Evidence: rust/lichen-node/src/dispatch.rs:301-303 handle_well_known_core returns only </sensors>,</config>,</deaddrop>,</confessions> — none of which have working handlers (deaddrop/confessions stubs return canned changed(), dispatch.rs:323-341; /config GET stub returns JSON {interval:60}, dispatch.rs:347-361); no Rust server handlers exist for /status, /status/neighbors, /status/routes, /keys, /config/radio, /config/identity; no Rust binary listens on 5683 as an LCI node server (lichend is a serial bridge); BLE service UUID is Meshtastic-style KISS 00000001-ba2a-46c9-ae49-01b0961f68bb (lichen-kiss/src/ble.rs:18) not NUS. Rust client-side models for all spec paths exist and are vector-tested (lichen-client/src/paths.rs, keystore.rs, status.rs). Suggested placement: implement Rust LCI server resources in lichen-node dispatch (or explicitly re-scope Rust to client/gateway role and fix WKC to advertise only existing resources); align BLE UUID or document KISS-over-BLE as the Rust transport binding in spec 17.3.2.
